23:1.sourceText: Τότε ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐλάλησεν τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ
23:1.targetText: Then Jesus spoke to the multitudes, and to His disciples,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.

23:2.sourceText: λέγων Ἐπὶ τῆς Μωϋσέως καθέδρας ἐκάθισαν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι.
23:2.targetText: saying, “On the seat of Moses sat down the scribes and the Pharisees;

23:3.sourceText: πάντα οὖν ὅσα ἐὰν εἴπωσιν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε καὶ τηρεῖτε, κατὰ δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν μὴ ποιεῖτε· λέγουσιν γὰρ καὶ οὐ ποιοῦσιν.
23:3.targetText: all, then, as much as they may say to you to observe, observe and do, but according to their works do not do, for they say, and do not do;

groups.note: N1904 orders the imperatives do and observe, whereas English orders observe and do. The actual doing and observing heads retain their correct English verbs rather than being swapped by position.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their works.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes a separate observing infinitive as the content of what they say; pinned N1904 has say to you followed by do and observe imperatives, without that additional written observing infinitive.

23:4.sourceText: δεσμεύουσιν δὲ φορτία βαρέα καὶ ἐπιτιθέασιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ὤμους τῶν ἀνθρώπων, αὐτοὶ δὲ τῷ δακτύλῳ αὐτῶν οὐ θέλουσιν κινῆσαι αὐτά.
23:4.targetText: for they bind together burdens [too] heavy and grievous to bear, and lay [them] on the shoulders of men, but with their finger they will not move them.

groups.note: The actual burdens are the objects of binding and the immediate coordinated laying action. English repeats the same real burdens as bracketed them; no second original pronoun is invented.
The actual dative article/finger constituent is instrumental, rendered with their finger. Its actual case governs the English relation without a separately printed with preposition.
The actual θέλω verb denotes willingness, rendered will in will not move; it is not a future auxiliary.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has δέ introducing the burden-binding statement; LSV follows a for introduction. The differing discourse connector is not relabeled as γάρ.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows a for introduction; the actual N1904 connective is δέ, not a printed γάρ.
English adds a degree marker too before heavy; no corresponding degree word is written in pinned N1904.
LSV includes the fuller difficult-to-bear description; pinned N1904 has heavy burdens without this added adjective/infinitive expression.

23:5.sourceText: πάντα δὲ τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ποιοῦσιν πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· πλατύνουσιν γὰρ τὰ φυλακτήρια αὐτῶν καὶ μεγαλύνουσιν τὰ κράσπεδα,
23:5.targetText: And all their works they do to be seen by men, and they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the fringes of their garments,

groups.note: The actual dative men phrase supplies the people by whom the works are seen, rendered by men. This is a case-governed viewer/agent relation, not a printed ὑπό preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with their works or their phylacteries.
N1904 has explanatory γάρ before making broad; LSV follows an and connector rather than that printed explanatory word.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows an and connector before making broad; pinned N1904 has γάρ, for, at that point.
LSV includes the garments phrase after fringes; pinned N1904 ends the phrase at fringes without a written garment noun or its possessor.

23:6.sourceText: φιλοῦσιν δὲ τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις καὶ τὰς πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς
23:6.targetText: they also cherish the first couches at the banquets, and the first seats in the synagogues,

groups.note: The actual connective δέ continues the description, rendered additively as also; the source remains δέ rather than a substituted καί particle.

23:7.sourceText: καὶ τοὺς ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ καλεῖσθαι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων Ῥαββεί.
23:7.targetText: and the salutations in the marketplaces, and to be called by men, Rabbi, Rabbi.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with men.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV repeats the Rabbi title, while pinned N1904 writes the title only once. The second English repetition is explicitly added rather than a second invented Greek title word.

23:8.sourceText: ὑμεῖς δὲ μὴ κληθῆτε Ῥαββεί· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ διδάσκαλος, πάντες δὲ ὑμεῖς ἀδελφοί ἐστε.
23:8.targetText: And you may not be called Rabbi, for one is your teacher—the Christ, and you are all brothers;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your teacher.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the Christ title after teacher; pinned N1904 has one is your teacher without that added title in this verse.

23:9.sourceText: καὶ πατέρα μὴ καλέσητε ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ Πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος.
23:9.targetText: and you may not call [any] your father on the earth, for one is your Father, who is in the heavens,

groups.note: The actual heavenly adjective οὐράνιος modifies Father, rendered in the heavens. It remains an adjective rather than a separate Greek heaven noun or be predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your Father.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an indefinite calling object any; no corresponding Greek indefinite object word is written here.
English supplies a relative copula before the heavenly adjective’s locative rendering; the original modifier has no corresponding be verb.

23:10.sourceText: μηδὲ κληθῆτε καθηγηταί, ὅτι καθηγητὴς ὑμῶν ἐστιν εἷς ὁ Χριστός.
23:10.targetText: nor may you be called teachers, for one is your teacher—the Christ.

groups.note: The actual καθηγητής is an instructor/guide head, rendered teachers, and is distinct from διδάσκαλος at23:8 despite the shared English teacher gloss.

23:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ μείζων ὑμῶν ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος.
23:11.targetText: And the greater of you will be your servant,

23:12.sourceText: Ὅστις δὲ ὑψώσει ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται, καὶ ὅστις ταπεινώσει ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.
23:12.targetText: and whoever will exalt himself will be humbled, and whoever will humble himself will be exalted.

23:13.sourceText: Οὐαὶ δὲ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι κλείετε τὴν βασιλείαν τῶν οὐρανῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ὑμεῖς γὰρ οὐκ εἰσέρχεσθε, οὐδὲ τοὺς εἰσερχομένους ἀφίετε εἰσελθεῖν.
23:13.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you shut up the kingdom of the heavens before men, for you do not go in, nor do you permit those going in to enter.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek δέ connective before the woe address is not separately expressed in this English verse.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with men.

23:14.targetText: [[Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you eat up the houses of the widows, and for a pretense make long prayers, because of this you will receive more abundant judgment.]]

unmappedTarget.text: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you eat up the houses of the widows, and for a pretense make long prayers, because of this you will receive more abundant judgment.
unmappedTarget.reason: The entire bracketed English verse is absent from the pinned N1904 Greek source witness. No source words or original anchors are invented for this verse.

review.note: LSV prints a bracketed verse23:14, but the pinned N1904 source contains no corresponding verse23:14.

23:15.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι περιάγετε τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηρὰν ποιῆσαι ἕνα προσήλυτον, καὶ ὅταν γένηται, ποιεῖτε αὐτὸν υἱὸν γεέννης διπλότερον ὑμῶν.
23:15.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you go around the sea and the dry land to make one proselyte, and whenever it may happen—you make him a son of Gehenna twofold more than yourselves.

23:16.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοὶ οἱ λέγοντες Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ ναῷ, οὐδέν ἐστιν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ χρυσῷ τοῦ ναοῦ, ὀφείλει.
23:16.targetText: Woe to you, blind guides, who are saying, Whoever may swear by the temple, it is nothing, but whoever may swear by the gold of the temple—is debtor!

groups.note: The actual ὀφείλω is the owing/obligation verb, rendered is debtor. The source is not a separate debtor noun or be predicate.

23:17.sourceText: μωροὶ καὶ τυφλοί, τίς γὰρ μείζων ἐστίν, ὁ χρυσὸς ἢ ὁ ναὸς ὁ ἁγιάσας τὸν χρυσόν;
23:17.targetText: Fools and blind! For which [is] greater, the gold, or the temple that is sanctifying the gold?

groups.note: The actual sanctifying participle ἁγιάσας is aorist active; English uses progressive is sanctifying. Its real verbal head retains the aorist participle form rather than a Greek present participle.

23:18.sourceText: καί Ὃς ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδέν ἐστιν· ὃς δ’ ἂν ὀμόσῃ ἐν τῷ δώρῳ τῷ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ, ὀφείλει.
23:18.targetText: And, Whoever may swear by the altar, it is nothing, but whoever may swear by the gift that is on it—is debtor!

groups.note: The actual owing verb ὀφείλει is rendered is debtor as a complete obligation predicate, without inventing a written Greek debtor noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative copula in the gift that is on it; Greek has an article-led locative modifier without a written be verb there.

23:19.sourceText: τυφλοί, τί γὰρ μεῖζον, τὸ δῶρον ἢ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ ἁγιάζον τὸ δῶρον;
23:19.targetText: Fools and blind! For which [is] greater, the gift, or the altar that is sanctifying the gift?

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds Fools and before blind; pinned N1904 begins this address with blind alone.
English supplies the main comparative copula; pinned N1904 has which greater without a written be verb here.

23:20.sourceText: ὁ οὖν ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ·
23:20.targetText: He therefore who swore by the altar, swears by it, and by all things on it;

groups.note: The actual all plus nominalizing article designates all the things on the altar; English all things retains that actual quantified nominal set without a separately written things noun.

23:21.sourceText: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ ναῷ ὀμνύει ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐν τῷ κατοικοῦντι αὐτόν·
23:21.targetText: and he who swore by the temple, swears by it, and by Him who is dwelling in it;

groups.note: The actual κατοικέω participle takes the inhabited temple as its accusative complement. English is dwelling in expresses the same habitation relation without a separately written in preposition or Greek be verb.
The actual masculine accusative αὐτόν refers to the temple being inhabited, rendered neutral English it; it is not a human Him object.

23:22.sourceText: καὶ ὁ ὀμόσας ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὀμνύει ἐν τῷ θρόνῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπάνω αὐτοῦ.
23:22.targetText: and he who swore by Heaven, swears by the throne of God, and by Him who is sitting on it.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with Heaven.

23:23.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι ἀποδεκατοῦτε τὸ ἡδύοσμον καὶ τὸ ἄνηθον καὶ τὸ κύμινον, καὶ ἀφήκατε τὰ βαρύτερα τοῦ νόμου, τὴν κρίσιν καὶ τὸ ἔλεος καὶ τὴν πίστιν· ταῦτα δὲ ἔδει ποιῆσαι κἀκεῖνα μὴ ἀφεῖναι.
23:23.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you give tithe of the mint, and the dill, and the cumin, and neglected the weightier things of the Law—judgment, and kindness, and faith; these it was necessary to do, and those not to neglect.

groups.note: The actual tithe-paying verb ἀποδεκατόω supplies you give tithe of, with the herb items as its objects. English tithe and of are part of the one verbal expression, not independent original noun/preposition heads.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with the English judgment, kindness and faith list.
The Greek δέ connective after these is not separately expressed in the English necessity clause.

23:24.sourceText: ὁδηγοὶ τυφλοί, οἱ διϋλίζοντες τὸν κώνωπα, τὴν δὲ κάμηλον καταπίνοντες.
23:24.targetText: Blind guides! Who are straining out the gnat, and are swallowing the camel.

23:25.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι καθαρίζετε τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ἐξ ἁρπαγῆς καὶ ἀκρασίας.
23:25.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you make clean the outside of the cup and the plate, and within they are full of robbery and self-indulgence.

23:26.sourceText: Φαρισαῖε τυφλέ, καθάρισον πρῶτον τὸ ἐντὸς τοῦ ποτηρίου ἵνα γένηται καὶ τὸ ἐκτὸς αὐτοῦ καθαρόν.
23:26.targetText: Blind Pharisee! First cleanse the inside of the cup and the plate, that the outside of them may also become clean.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has singular αὐτοῦ, of it, for the cup’s outside; LSV follows plural of them after its fuller cup-and-plate wording. The actual singular pronoun is not relabeled as a plural.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the additional plate phrase; pinned N1904 mentions only the inside of the cup here.
LSV follows a plural possessor with the fuller cup/plate phrase; pinned N1904 has singular αὐτοῦ for the cup’s outside.

23:27.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι παρομοιάζετε τάφοις κεκονιαμένοις, οἵτινες ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνονται ὡραῖοι, ἔσωθεν δὲ γέμουσιν ὀστέων νεκρῶν καὶ πάσης ἀκαθαρσίας.
23:27.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you are like to whitewashed graves, which outwardly indeed appear beautiful, and within are full of bones of dead men, and of all uncleanness;

groups.note: The actual resemblance verb παρομοιάζω supplies you are like; its English copula belongs to the real resemblance predicate rather than an unwritten Greek be verb.

23:28.sourceText: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔξωθεν μὲν φαίνεσθε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δίκαιοι, ἔσωθεν δέ ἐστε μεστοὶ ὑποκρίσεως καὶ ἀνομίας.
23:28.targetText: so also you outwardly indeed appear to men righteous, and within you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.

23:29.sourceText: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, γραμματεῖς καὶ Φαρισαῖοι ὑποκριταί, ὅτι οἰκοδομεῖτε τοὺς τάφους τῶν προφητῶν καὶ κοσμεῖτε τὰ μνημεῖα τῶν δικαίων,
23:29.targetText: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! Because you build the graves of the prophets, and adorn the tombs of the righteous,

23:30.sourceText: καὶ λέγετε Εἰ ἤμεθα ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν, οὐκ ἂν ἤμεθα αὐτῶν κοινωνοὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι τῶν προφητῶν.
23:30.targetText: and say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets.

groups.note: The actual imperfect be form ἤμεθα appears in the unreal past condition, rendered we had been. Its written form remains imperfect rather than a Greek pluperfect.
The actual modal ἄν with the imperfect be verb supplies the contrary-to-fact we would have been result; both source items remain together rather than a fabricated future form.
The actual genitive αὐτῶν marks the companions in the partaker construction, rendered with them. Its source case remains genitive rather than an invented with preposition.

23:31.sourceText: ὥστε μαρτυρεῖτε ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι υἱοί ἐστε τῶν φονευσάντων τοὺς προφήτας.
23:31.targetText: So that you testify to yourselves that you are sons of them who murdered the prophets;

23:32.sourceText: καὶ ὑμεῖς πληρώσατε τὸ μέτρον τῶν πατέρων ὑμῶν.
23:32.targetText: and you fill up the measure of your fathers.

groups.note: The actual πληρώσατε is an aorist imperative, rendered you fill up. The source retains its imperative form rather than an indicative prediction.

23:33.sourceText: ὄφεις, γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, πῶς φύγητε ἀπὸ τῆς κρίσεως τῆς γεέννης;
23:33.targetText: Serpents! Brood of vipers! How may you escape from the judgment of Gehenna?

23:34.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω πρὸς ὑμᾶς προφήτας καὶ σοφοὺς καὶ γραμματεῖς· ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀποκτενεῖτε καὶ σταυρώσετε, καὶ ἐξ αὐτῶν μαστιγώσετε ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ὑμῶν καὶ διώξετε ἀπὸ πόλεως εἰς πόλιν·
23:34.targetText: Because of this, behold, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and scribes, and of them you will kill and crucify, and of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and will pursue from city to city,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your synagogues.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a conjunction before the first of-them clause; pinned N1904 has a direct of-them continuation after the scribes list without that extra conjunction.

23:35.sourceText: ὅπως ἔλθῃ ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς πᾶν αἷμα δίκαιον ἐκχυννόμενον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος Ἅβελ τοῦ δικαίου ἕως τοῦ αἵματος Ζαχαρίου υἱοῦ Βαραχίου, ὃν ἐφονεύσατε μεταξὺ τοῦ ναοῦ καὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου.
23:35.targetText: that on you may come all the righteous blood being poured out on the earth from the blood of Abel the righteous, to the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom you murdered between the temple and the altar:

23:36.sourceText: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἥξει ταῦτα πάντα ἐπὶ τὴν γενεὰν ταύτην.
23:36.targetText: truly I say to you, all these things will come on this generation.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with this generation.

23:37.sourceText: Ἰερουσαλὴμ Ἰερουσαλήμ, ἡ ἀποκτείνουσα τοὺς προφήτας καὶ λιθοβολοῦσα τοὺς ἀπεσταλμένους πρὸς αὐτήν, ποσάκις ἠθέλησα ἐπισυναγαγεῖν τὰ τέκνα σου, ὃν τρόπον ὄρνις ἐπισυνάγει τὰ νοσσία αὐτῆς ὑπὸ τὰς πτέρυγας, καὶ οὐκ ἠθελήσατε.
23:37.targetText: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, that are killing the prophets, and stoning those sent to you, how often I willed to gather your children together, as a hen gathers her own chickens under the wings, and you did not will.

groups.note: The actual θέλω verb expresses willing/wanting to gather, not a future auxiliary.
The actual θέλω verb expresses refusal of will, rendered you did not will. It is not a separate future auxiliary.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has the third-person singular αὐτήν, to her, for Jerusalem as the sending destination; LSV addresses that destination as second-person you. The actual person forms remain distinct.
The Greek articles are not separately expressed with your children or her chickens.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows a second-person sending destination; pinned N1904 has the third-person αὐτήν, her, in to-her.
LSV explicitly emphasizes her own chickens; pinned N1904 writes the ordinary αὐτῆς, her, without a distinct own adjective or reflexive possessive form there.

23:38.sourceText: ἰδοὺ ἀφίεται ὑμῖν ὁ οἶκος ὑμῶν.
23:38.targetText: Behold, your house is left to you desolate;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with your house.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes the desolate predicate adjective; pinned N1904 has your house is left to you without a written desolate adjective.

23:39.sourceText: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν, οὐ μή με ἴδητε ἀπ’ ἄρτι ἕως ἂν εἴπητε Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου.
23:39.targetText: for I say to you, you may not see Me from now on, until you may say, Blessed [is] He who is coming in the Name of the LORD.”

groups.note: The actual perfect passive blessing participle supplies the English Blessed-is predicate; its auxiliary belongs to this real verbal passive expression, not an independently printed Greek be verb.
